programme: RFX5 drives the CIITA-dependent MHC class II transactivation complex (its target list is almost entirely HLA-DR/DP/DQ/DM/DO plus CIITA itself) while TCF3 (E2A) runs the pre-BCR/B-lymphocyte differentiation programme (CD79A, CD79B, VPREB1, IGLL1, PAX5, PTCRA); MSC (musculin) is the canonical E-protein antagonist that heterodimerizes with TCF3/E2A products to dampen that same lymphocyte-differentiation output, and CTCF (which also binds its own partner RAD21, plus HLA-E, IL4, CISH, CD34) supplies chromatin architecture at antigen-receptor and MHC loci. Together these four describe a coordinated antigen-presentation / lymphocyte-differentiation regulon, not a single physical complex.
role_in_a: In fibromyalgia (blood), this regulon would run in circulating immune cells: RFX5/CIITA setting HLA class II presentation capacity and TCF3/MSC setting B-lineage output. Immune dysregulation is a minority, emerging theme in fibromyalgia (small-fiber neuropathy, altered cytokines) rather than an established disease mechanism.
role_in_b: In IBS (colorectal), the same regulon would run in gut-associated lymphoid tissue and colonic mucosa, consistent with the recognized theme of mucosal immune activation and altered mucosal lymphocyte populations in post-infectious and diarrhea-predominant IBS.
shared_axis: Fibromyalgia and IBS are well-documented comorbid 'central sensitization' / functional somatic syndromes with a proposed gut-brain-immune axis; if RFX5-driven MHC-II presentation and the TCF3/MSC lymphocyte-differentiation balance are concordantly engaged in both the blood and gut compartments across patient subgroups, that would point to a shared low-grade adaptive-immune activation underlying part of their comorbidity, rather than a mechanism specific to either tissue.
reasoning: The programme is nameable from textbook immunology (RFX5/CIITA for MHC-II, TCF3/MSC as an E-protein pair, CTCF as their architectural partner), and the fibromyalgia-IBS pairing itself is a recognized clinical comorbidity, so the connection follows from reasoning rather than anatomy being surprising. But the retrieved record barely touches it: Open Targets shows no real association for any of the four factors in either disease (CTCF's IBS percentile of 0.07 is noise-level), no PMID ties RFX5 to either disease, and the strongest-looking literature (MSC) turns out to be about mesenchymal stem cell therapy, an unrelated entity sharing the gene symbol.
support: 39073655 — reviews TCF3 mutations and immune dysfunction, listing IBS only as a GI symptom in affected patients; link to TCF3's regulatory role is unclear. 38662876 — describes 'CTCF-related disorder', a rare congenital CTCF-haploinsufficiency syndrome in which IBS is a listed feature; not evidence for the antigen-presentation/lymphocyte module itself. 40353645, 41484803, 34377093, 41480397, 40691643, 40740529 — all discuss mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy in fibromyalgia or IBS; this is the cell-therapy entity, not the MSC/musculin transcription factor scored here, so despite the symbol match these do not support the account. No literature was retrieved for RFX5 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In matched blood (fibromyalgia) and colonic mucosal (IBS) samples versus healthy controls, measure HLA-DR/DP/DQ surface expression on antigen-presenting cells and CD79A+/PAX5+ pre-B/B-cell frequencies by flow cytometry or scRNA-seq; if RFX5-driven MHC-II expression and TCF3-dependent B-lineage output are not concordantly shifted relative to controls in both conditions, the shared-module claim is falsified. A complementary test: RFX5 or TCF3 knockdown in a relevant immune cell line should co-regulate HLA-II and pre-BCR gene sets together — if they vary independently of each other, the proposed single regulon does not hold.
caveats: The 16 patient-group comparisons come from only 1 independent cohort pair (blood vs colorectal), so this could reflect one cohort's technical signature rather than replicated biology. PAX8, BARX2, HOXC9, CAMTA1, DMAP1, SPDEF and PLAGL2 recur at similar or higher counts (up to 12/16) but do not fit this or any other coherent module (thyroid, neural-crest/ECM, developmental patterning, generic epigenetic machinery, goblet-cell) and were deliberately left out — a reminder that recurrence alone does not imply a shared mechanism. EBF1, TCF3's usual B-lymphopoiesis partner, was removed as tissue-generic, so the B-lineage half of this account is less complete than a textbook description would be. Classic generic immune regulators (SPI1/PU.1, STAT3, ETS1, RELB, FOXO3, KLF9, FLI1, TWIST1, GLI1) were also removed as tissue-generic, and PBX1 was single-view (one patient group only) — neither exclusion list undercuts the account since none of those factors were used, but it does mean this story rests on only 4 of the 12 surviving factors.
